summary: Communicates with external serial devices over RS-232-style ports, logging received bytes, lines, or messages and sending bytes through Python or Tscript methods.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enable the serial connection

key_params.name: format
key_params.note: Append one row per byte, per line, or per full message

key_params.name: port
key_params.note: COM or serial port name used for the connection

key_params.name: baudrate
key_params.note: Serial baud rate for the device connection

key_params.name: databits

key_params.note: Serial parity bit mode

common_gotchas: USB serial adapters require OS drivers and correct port names before the DAT can connect.
Per Line mode does not append a row until newline, carriage return, or null termination arrives.
Baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, DTR, and RTS must match the device or data can appear corrupt or absent.
Callbacks execute once per received message and can be high frequency in per-byte mode.
The output table is a receive log; outgoing data is sent with serialDAT Python/Tscript send methods.
key_concepts: Reads and writes serial-port data into a DAT event table.
Port, baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, DTR, and RTS configure the serial connection.
Format and Bytes controls determine how received serial data is represented.
Callbacks and FIFO retention controls manage incoming serial messages.
